reply_text:
I found no dated AI predictions by Shane Legg from 2013. I ran all three fixed searches, then 9 more searches and 3 page openings, so I used all 12 searches and half the 6 page openings. DeepMind was still in stealth that year and nothing turned up in his own words from 2013.

- **Nothing turned up from 2013.** The only 2013 mention was in a search snippet of the Dwarkesh podcast transcript (2023): Legg recalls DeepMind's first safety hire "Back in 2013 or so". That's a later retelling with no prediction in it, and I didn't open the page.
- **The Despres interview (future.fandom.com) has no date, so it can't be counted for 2013.** I opened it. It contains timeline predictions: "Human level AI will be passed in the mid 2020's" and, for things getting "really crazy" after human-level AGI, "some time from 2025 to 2040". He describes his current work as including "cognitive bias in financial markets", which points to before DeepMind, roughly 2009–10, but I'm inferring that.
- **Other years:**
  - The LessWrong Q&A he's best known for is dated 17 June 2011 in the Wikipedia citation (I didn't open the post).
  - An arXiv paper quotes his last year-end forecast ("a log-normal distribution with a mean of 2028 and a mode of 2025"). I saw that only in a search snippet and didn't open the paper or his vetta.org blog post. My attempt to open vetta.org was refused because the address hadn't appeared in my search results first.
  - The Oxford Martin talk was 10 March 2010 and the UKH+ lecture was 31 October 2009, according to search snippets. Neither page was opened, and neither snippet contained a prediction.
